description: New Hampshire-only rules checked against the cited Revised Statutes Annotated. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: In a posted New Hampshire school zone, the prima facie limit is
options: 10 mph below the usual posted limit
the same as the usual posted limit
questions.explanation: RSA 265:60, II(a) sets a posted school zone at 10 miles per hour below the usual posted limit from 45 minutes prior to each school opening until opening and from each closing until 45 minutes after closing.

questions.q: Where no lower speed is required, New Hampshire's prima facie limit in a business or urban residence district is
questions.explanation: RSA 265:60, II(b) sets 30 miles per hour in any business or urban residence district as defined in RSA 259:118. A speed over that limit is prima facie evidence the speed is not reasonable or prudent.

questions.q: New Hampshire's prima facie limit in a rural residence district, and on a class V highway outside the compact part of a city or town, is
questions.explanation: RSA 265:60, II(c) sets 35 miles per hour in any rural residence district as defined in RSA 259:93, and on any class V highway outside the compact part of a city or town as defined in RSA 229:5, IV.

questions.q: On a 4-lane divided interstate or the central or eastern New Hampshire turnpike, the maximum lawful speed is
options: 75 mph if the road is rural
questions.explanation: RSA 265:60, II(f) sets 65 miles an hour on the interstate system and the central and eastern New Hampshire turnpikes where they are 4-lane divided highways or other divided highways of 4 or more lanes, except 70 miles per hour on I-93 from mile marker 45 to the Vermont border. Paragraph III makes the II(f) limits a maximum lawful speed, not only a prima facie limit. Other roads may be posted differently under RSA 265:62.

questions.q: New Hampshire forbids driving with an alcohol concentration of
questions.explanation: RSA 265-A:2, I(b) prohibits driving a vehicle on any way while the person has an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more, or, if the person is under 21, 0.02 or more.

questions.q: A New Hampshire driver under 21 violates the alcohol-concentration rule at
options: 0.08, the same number as an adult
questions.explanation: RSA 265-A:2, I(b) states the under-21 alcohol concentration as 0.02 or more. The adult figure in the same paragraph is 0.08.

questions.q: A New Hampshire commercial-license holder who drives a commercial vehicle at an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or greater
options: has broken no extra rule if the result is under 0.08
is subject to the additional penalties and sanctions in RSA 263:94
loses the commercial license for 10 days only
is treated the same as a driver with no alcohol
questions.explanation: RSA 265-A:23 says a holder of a commercial driver license or endorsement who is convicted of RSA 265-A:2 or 265-A:3, or who drives a commercial vehicle with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or greater, is subject, in addition to the penalties in that chapter, to the additional penalties and sanctions in RSA 263:94.

questions.q: For a New Hampshire driver 21 or older, the DMV may suspend the license for up to 3 months after
options: 12 demerit points in one calendar year
Nothing: New Hampshire has no point system
questions.explanation: New Hampshire DMV rule Saf-C 212.02 sets demerit-point suspensions by age. At 21 and older: 12 points in one calendar year (up to 3 months), 18 in two years (up to 6 months), 24 in three years (up to 1 year). Drivers under 21 face lower totals.

questions.q: New Hampshire certifies a habitual offender for serious offenses when, within 5 years, the record shows
questions.explanation: RSA 259:39, I certifies a habitual offender for three or more convictions, within 5 years based on the date of the offense, of the serious offenses listed there. Those include an offense involving a vehicle under RSA 265-A:2, I, and under RSA 265-A:3.

questions.q: A mixed New Hampshire habitual-offender record, within 5 years, is
options: one paragraph I plus 8 paragraph II convictions
12 points of any type, with no conviction needed
questions.explanation: RSA 259:39, III certifies a habitual offender for that combination of one serious conviction plus at least 8 of the paragraph II offenses, or two serious convictions plus at least 4 paragraph II offenses, within the 5-year period.

questions.q: For New Hampshire habitual-offender counting, the 5-year window is measured by
options: the date the license was issued
the calendar year of the birthday
a rolling 12 months of demerit points
questions.explanation: RSA 259:39 says the convictions must have been committed within a 5-year period, based on the date of the offense. It is a conviction count, not a demerit-point total.

questions.q: New Hampshire issues a youth operator's license to applicants who are
questions.explanation: RSA 263:14, II(a) requires a youth operator's license for applicants 16 or older and under 21. It expires on the 21st anniversary of the applicant's date of birth. An applicant under 18 also needs RSA 263:17 or written parental consent plus the driver-education certificate in RSA 263:19.

questions.q: A New Hampshire youth operator who is not over 18 shall not drive
questions.explanation: RSA 263:14, II(b) says the holder shall not operate between 1:00 a.m. and 4:00 a.m., and shall not operate when occupants exceed the number of safety restraints. Paragraph II(f) says the restrictions in II(b), II(c), and II(d) do not apply to drivers who are over 18.

questions.q: During the first 6 months, a New Hampshire youth operator shall not drive with
options: more than one unrelated passenger under 25
more than three passengers of any age
questions.explanation: RSA 263:14, II(c) limits the first 6 months to no more than one passenger less than 25 who is not a member of the holder's family, unless the driver is accompanied by a licensed responsible adult who is at least 25. Paragraph II(f) drops that restriction for drivers over 18.

questions.q: A person under 18 who wants a New Hampshire license under RSA 263:19 must, besides an approved driver-education course, certify
options: 40 more supervised hours, 10 of them at night
50 hours including 10 at night with any adult
questions.explanation: RSA 263:19, II requires certification of 40 hours of additional supervised driving under a licensed parent or guardian, or if none, a licensed adult over 25, with at least 10 of those hours from one-half hour after sunset to one-half hour before sunrise. Paragraph I separately requires an approved course of at least 30 hours of classroom instruction, 10 hours behind the wheel, and 6 hours of observation.

questions.q: In New Hampshire, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: New Hampshire issues a learner's permit for a car at 15½ years at the earliest.
questions.remember: New Hampshire car permit: 15½ years at the earliest.

provenance.manual: State of New Hampshire Driver Manual

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in New Hampshire complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: New Hampshire requires 40 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.
questions.remember: New Hampshire: 40 hours of supervised driving.

questions.q: Of a New Hampshire teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: New Hampshire requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.
questions.remember: New Hampshire: 10 hours of the supervised driving at night.

provenance.manual: Driver Education | NH Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: In New Hampshire, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In New Hampshire, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.
questions.remember: New Hampshire: driving alone from 16 years.

questions.q: In New Hampshire, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: New Hampshire drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 18 years.

provenance.manual: Driver Licensing Requirements for Minors | NH Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: How many questions are on the New Hampshire car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The New Hampshire car knowledge test has 40 questions.

provenance.manual: State of New Hampshire Driver Manual

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the New Hampshire car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the New Hampshire car knowledge test.
questions.remember: New Hampshire car test: pass with 80%.

provenance.manual: Driver Licensing Testing Requirements | NH Division of Motor Vehicles

questions.q: In New Hampshire, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in New Hampshire brings a suspension of 180 days.
questions.remember: New Hampshire, first refusal: 180 days without a license.

provenance.manual: State of New Hampshire Driver Manual

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in New Hampshire?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in New Hampshire can be posted up to 70 mph for cars.
questions.remember: New Hampshire rural interstate: up to 70 mph.

provenance.manual: State of New Hampshire Driver Manual

questions.q: Which best describes New Hampshire's law on drivers using a phone?
options: Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Only texting is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: New Hampshire: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.
questions.remember: New Hampshire phone law: hands-free only.

provenance.manual: State of New Hampshire Driver Manual

questions.q: How is New Hampshire's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: No seat belt law for adults
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
questions.explanation: New Hampshire seat belt enforcement is no seat belt law for adults.
questions.remember: New Hampshire: no adult seat belt law.

provenance.manual: State of New Hampshire Driver Manual

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in New Hampshire?
questions.explanation: New Hampshire requires a car seat or booster until 7 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: New Hampshire: car or booster seat until 7 years.
